title: A Thorn for the Sigil Revisited
premise: August Delacroix keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories and impossible things, until a dying courier presses a bloodstained map into her hands — a map that shows the thirteenth moon, the one that will complete its turn and seal King Aldric's soul beneath the sigil wearing his crown. Hunted by the guild she served, courted by rebels who want the throne broken, August must gather a found family of outcasts to reach the Moonvault beneath the capital. There she discovers the map was bait: the sigil itself chose her, because memory-thieves are the only ones who can unbind it without killing the king. In the end August pays the price of survival by surrendering her own dearest memories to shatter the sigil, freeing Aldric but forgetting the people who became her family — until they refuse to let her carry that loss alone.
about_author: August Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction. They write from a cluttered study in a coastal town, where they insist every story is just a ledger of debts someone finally came to collect.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV August. A night in the Vellum Guild's counting house: August balances accounts of traded memories, glimpsing the guild's quiet cruelties. She pockets one memory vial she shouldn't. Emotional beat: wary competence masking loneliness; establishes her rules and her small rebellions.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: POV August. A bleeding courier collapses into her rooms, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'thirteen turns' before dying. Guild enforcers arrive minutes behind him. August flees through the rooftops with the map. Beat: terror and reluctant commitment; her old life burns behind her.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: POV August. Hiding in a smuggler's cellar, August studies the map: routes to the Moonvault beneath the palace, annotated in her own dead mother's handwriting. The guild posts her likeness. Beat: grief entangled with suspicion — why would her mother's hand be on this?

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: POV Sable, guild enforcer and August's former mentor. Sable is ordered to retrieve the map and erase August. She hesitates, remembering the girl she trained. Beat: cold duty cracking against affection; introduces the antagonist's humanity.

chapters.title: Thieves, Liars, and One Very Large Dog
chapters.summary: POV August. August recruits help: Bramble, a disgraced palace locksmith; Wren, a child pickpocket who knows the sewers; and Ossian, an ex-soldier whose memories were sold to pay his unit's debts. Beat: found family begins to assemble around shared damage.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: POV Ossian. The new moon rises — turn one of thirteen. Ossian feels the sigil's pull through his stolen-memory scars. He confesses he once guarded the king and remembers nothing of the year he served. Beat: dread; the clock starts ticking for everyone.

chapters.title: Market of Whispers
chapters.summary: POV August. To learn what the sigil is, August trades a precious memory of her mother to a black-market oracle. She learns the sigil is a parasite that eats kings slowly, and that it fears memory-thieves. Beat: sacrifice establishing theme — survival always costs something kept.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable corners August alone and offers amnesty if she surrenders the map, revealing the guild master serves the sigil willingly. August refuses. Their fight is more argument than blades. Beat: heartbreak between mentor and student; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Under the Capital
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren leads the group through drowned catacombs toward the palace foundations. Traps, rising water, and Wren's fear of being abandoned again. Beat: trust tested under pressure; Wren chooses the family over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV August. Disguised as servants, they witness King Aldric at court — lucid for one terrible minute, begging a stranger to kill him before the moon turns. The sigil notices August's talent. Beat: horror and pity; the enemy has a hostage face.

chapters.title: Bramble's Locks
chapters.summary: POV Bramble. Bramble picks the vault gate that exiled him years ago, confronting the master who ruined him. He wins them entry but takes a wound that fester-worries Ossian. Beat: vindication shadowed by cost; no door opens free.

chapters.title: Turn Seven
chapters.summary: POV Ossian. Halfway through the moon's cycle, Ossian's scars begin showing fragments of his erased year — including orders he gave that killed civilians. He spirals; August anchors him by sharing her own guilt. Beat: the price of survival is remembering what you'd rather forget.

chapters.title: The Guild Master's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV August. Captured briefly by guild agents, August reads the master's private ledger: her mother didn't make the map — she stole it, and died for it. August escapes with the truth and a burning question about her own childhood sale. Beat: rage reforged into purpose.

chapters.title: What August Sold
chapters.summary: POV August. Flashback chapter braided with present: August discovers she sold her own memories of her mother voluntarily, years ago, to buy Bramble's freedom from the guild. Beat: devastating reveal — her family debts were paid in family.

chapters.title: Sable Turns Her Coat
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Reading the same ledger, Sable realizes the guild master intends to feed the whole city's memories to the sigil on the final turn. She defects, bringing guild keys and her blade. Beat: redemption earned, not given; uneasy alliance sealed in blood.

chapters.title: The Descent to the Moonvault
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The full company breaches the vault approach as turn eleven wanes. The sigil fights back with illusions drawn from their own memories — each must walk past a perfect lie. Beat: climax approach; everyone names what tempts them and refuses it.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve: The Bargain
chapters.summary: POV August. In the vault's antechamber, the sigil speaks through the guild master's mouth: leave now, keep your memories, live rich. August understands the map was bait to deliver a thief capable of unbinding it safely. Beat: temptation at maximum; she chooses the hard road aloud.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV August. Climax. August enters the king's mind and unpicks the sigil stitch by stitch while it devours her memories in retaliation — her mother's face, the guild years, then the faces of her new family. Ossian and Sable hold her body steady. Beat: agonizing triumph; she wins by giving everything.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Crown
chapters.summary: POV Ossian. The sigil dies; Aldric wakes weeping and human; the guild master is taken alive by Sable's evidence. But August wakes blank-eyed among strangers, not knowing any of them. Beat: hollow victory; the cost lands on the page.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Stay
chapters.summary: POV Wren. The family refuses to let August face her loss alone. Wren decides they'll simply tell her everything, daily, until the stories take root. Small scenes of re-introduction: tea, the dog, the ledger rewritten together. Beat: tenderness after ruin; love as deliberate practice.

chapters.title: A Memory Returned
chapters.summary: POV August. Among the sigil's remains, August finds one vial it couldn't digest: her mother's voice, saying her name. Drinking it doesn't restore the past but gives her an anchor — proof she was loved and chose rightly. Beat: bittersweet grace; some prices are survivable.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: POV August. Epilogue. The old guild is dissolved; August opens a new house that returns stolen memories instead of trading them, with Sable as warden, Bramble as locksmith, Ossian as guard, Wren as apprentice. Under the first moon of a clean count, she writes the opening line: all debts begin here. Beat: hopeful resolution; found family made permanent.
